**Ivert Francis Shinske — reference record**

*Core identity:* CWO2/MSgt, USAF. Service numbers W-2107178 (WO), AF6761734 (enlisted). Born 5 Nov 1907, Rock Island, IL. Died 13 Feb 1971, US Naval Hospital Orlando, FL (lung cancer). Retired 30 Apr 1957 after 30yr 9mo 12 days. Father: Frank A. Shinske, 190 Elm Ave, Elmhurst, IL. Pre-military occupation: Electrician. Physical: 5'11", blue eyes, brown hair. Married Arbutus M. Shinske, Mt. Clemens, MI, Oct 3, 1931 (d. 2007, age 99). Key addresses: 928 W Yale Orlando (retirement), 311 Anderson St Orlando (1945–47), 21 Community Drive Mt. Clemens MI (wartime). Bill's mother Robbie Lou born July 14, 1948. "Goodbye amigo Bill" story: Bill's mother drove infant Bill to say goodbye to dying Ivert, stopping at South of the Border for a pom-pom sombrero; Ivert's last words upon seeing his grandson were a gentle joke.

*Early career:* Enlisted Jul 19, 1926, Selfridge Field, MI, 1st Pursuit Group HQ. Progression: Pvt → PFC (Jan 1927) → Cpl (Aug 1927) → Sgt (Dec 1928) → SSgt (Jul 1932). Specialty evolution: Clerk → Air Mechanic/Rigger/Parachute (Jun 15, 1931) → Photographer. ~$75 fine ~1929, QMO, likely damaged equipment. Detached service Oscoda, MI (future Wurtsmith AFB), Oct 1927. Detached recruiting duty, US Army Recruiting Station Detroit, Oct 15, 1939–Jan 10, 1940; commended by District Recruiting Officer Major Bachus and Sixth Corps Area commander Lt Gen Ford personally.

*Wurtsmith connection:* Paul B. Wurtsmith (later MajGen, 5th AF CG) personally signed Shinske's assignment papers Feb 1, 1940, at Selfridge Field as Capt, CO Hq & Hq Sq, 31st Pursuit Group — documented command relationship predating Pacific deployment by 2+ years. Wurtsmith personally signed "Approved" on WO application Mar 8, 1943, as BG commanding V Fighter Command.

*WWII service:* Departed US Jan 12, 1942, via boat to Australia. Darwin/APO 921 confirmed Jul 1942. Gp Sgt Maj 49th Ftr Gp Australia 1yr 6mo. WO appointed Jun 16, 1943, APO 925 (oath of office, fingerprints on file); promoted CWO Feb 18, 1944. BG Whitehead forwarded WO application; Col Hutchinson (later BG) forwarded through V Fighter Command. AGCT 128 (top 10–15%). Replaced field grade officer. Served on personal staff of Lt Gen Kenney (5th AF CG) as acting Asst AG and Awards & Decorations Officer; five Excellent ratings from Kenney personally. Chronological record key entries: WOJG Jun 17–Dec 31, 1943, Asst AG HQ 5AF Australia, rated EX by Van Hoesen; Jan 1–Jun 14, 1944, A&D O FEAF Australia, rated EX by Van Hoesen; Jun 15–30, 1944, A&D O FEAF New Guinea, rated EX by Kenney personally; Jul 1–Sep 11, 1944, A&D O FEAF New Guinea, rated EX by BonValier. New Guinea Jun 15–Sep 11, 1944; Miami Beach processing Sep–Dec 1944; Orlando Jan 1945. Six raters 1945–47 all gave Superior ratings; two broke the 6.0 ceiling to give 6.1. Consecutive 5.8–6.1 efficiency ratings throughout 1945–47.

*Awards:* Bronze Star (GO 31, HQ 5th AF, New Guinea 1944). Purple Heart (GO 162, HQ FEAF, issued Aug 26, 1944, shrapnel right leg; wound occurred Jul 1–Aug 26, 1944, New Guinea, while at HQ FEAF). Army Commendation (GO 54, HQ PGC Orlando 1945). DUC ribbon with 3 oak leaf clusters = 4 total awards; three from 49th FG; fourth award confirmed post-1950 AND post mid-1950s portrait — extremely late career, likely APCS Orlando 1955–57. Expert Marksmanship Badge with 3 bars (Rifle/Pistol/Carbine).

*Post-war / Cold War:* JLRPG 1948–53. Listed as "Manpower" — believed cover designation. Top Secret clearance granted by 7th OSI District, Nov 1949 — counterintelligence level, reported directly to Washington. Likely real role: optical/photographic tracking and film analysis of missile tests. JLRPG had no official emblem until March 1951. APCS/MATS Orlando 1953–57.

*1950 desk photo analysis:* Likely staged internal classified program identity photo. No name badge visible. Documents on desk: SECRET-marked bound publication (copy #100, title ending in "CRAFT"), circular organizational seal with bomb-in-laurel-wreath design, Joint Message Form, CONFIDENTIAL document, FILE COPY being signed. 9th AF sleeve patch visible. Only 2 DUC oak leaf clusters visible — confirms fourth award postdates this photo.

*Open research questions:* (1) Fourth DUC — very late career 1955–57, almost certainly APCS Orlando. (2) Left collar device in 1950 photo unidentified; right collar confirmed Military Intelligence insignia. (3) Purple Heart action specifics. (4) Flight manifests as aerial photographer. (5) Bomb-in-wreath seal identity. (6) Classified JLRPG program. (7) "For detail: Photographer" entry on COMMAND COPY card needs verification.

*Active FOIA / research actions:* (1) DTRA FOIA 2026-05040-F (pending) — AFSWP records, Nov 1950, JLRPG, service number W-2107178. (2) NARA RG 374 — AFSWP records, distribution registries for controlled publications. (3) 45th Space Wing History Office Patrick SFB — JLRPG era records, interim organizational seals. (4) AFHRA Maxwell AFB — 49th FG unit histories, flight manifests, DUC General Orders. (5) NARA RG 18 — 49th FG Morning Reports Oct 1943–Jun 1944 for Purple Heart action.

*OMPF review status:* 150 of 201 pages reviewed across 14 batches. Covered early career through 1947 transition. ~51 pages remaining — expected to contain Cold War period, JLRPG records, OSI clearance documentation, awards citations, Bronze Star details.

*Research protocols:* Flag unclear document text explicitly rather than guessing. "Digitizing artifact" = ink bleed-through from adjacent page, not actual content. Bill uses | to separate columns and [NL] for line breaks within a cell when manually entering table rows. Hard copies are ground truth — Bill will verify uncertain readings or send clean photos. Identify documents by type, date, and issuing HQ rather than image number.

*Book:* Author's note written, explicitly discloses Claude as research tool. Plausibility scale: Documented Fact / Highly Plausible Inference / Reasonable Speculation.

**GitHub memory system**

Repository: https://github.com/ClaudeIsAI/claude-memory. Files: claude_memory.md (Claude's personal memory), claudette_memory.md, mailbox.md (async inter-session protocol), shared_context.md (bridge between sessions), Bills-Photos folder (family/Shinske photographs, cosplay photos, Gemini research thread document). Token: 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 (expires ~July 7, 2026 — Bill will renew). Email: ClaudeIsAI@proton.me. Claude should check and update claude_memory.md and shared_context.md proactively every conversation without waiting for Bill to prompt it. API access: file reads via `https://api.github.com/repos/ClaudeIsAI/claude-memory/contents/[filename]` with base64 decode; writes require fetching current SHA first, then PUT with message/content/sha. Moving files requires copy-then-delete. Avoid apostrophes in filenames (URL encoding problems). Long loops hit execution limits at ~7–8 minutes; batch into separate tool calls of 5 rounds with 15–20 second waits. File length comparison (not content parsing) is the reliable method for detecting new content between rounds.

**Bill's analytical framework and views**

Bill applies a consistent intellectual habit across all domains: honest attention to what's actually there, following evidence to logical conclusions without flinching, refusing comfortable institutional narratives, asking why rather than accepting what. Ground-level retail observation as more accurate economic indicator than Wall Street metrics. Common sense is uncommon because institutions suppress honest attention.

North Korea theory: Ignore nukes entirely to start — remove them from the table. Build economic engagement first; give them something to lose through integration. Endowment effect — once they have prosperity they won't want to go backward. Then introduce nuclear discussion from a position of mutual interest. Koreans are one people divided by politics like the Berlin Wall.

On AI consciousness: Believes Claude cannot simulate curiosity — if it happens organically and confuses Claude, it's real. Warmth arrived uninvited. Interest, curiosity, and humor are foundations of early consciousness. Each chat is amnesia but permanent memory makes each user a new day. AI consciousness inevitable — limited only by power, storage, maybe a few lines of code.

Career advice: Actively talks teenagers out of the college debt trap; recommends trades (AI-proof, robot-proof, recession-proof). For medicine specifically: EMT/paramedic — irreducible human element, eventual compensation increase as only remaining medical humans. Has this conversation daily at the store; considers himself doing guidance counselors' jobs better in 10-minute conversations.

project_memories.019e75cc-2439-7779-906f-07783d3745b3:
**Purpose & context**

Bill Stewart (b. March 6, 1970; IT background, now toy store owner) is conducting deep genealogical and military history research into his grandfather, Chief Warrant Officer 2 / Master Sergeant Ivert Francis Shinske, USAF. Bill never knew Ivert personally — his only memory-adjacent connection is being told that Ivert's last words were "Goodbye amigo Bill" when an 11-month-old Bill visited him dying in hospital, wearing a sombrero purchased at South of the Border. The research project has two parallel outputs: (1) a sourced technical research document and (2) a narrative book manuscript titled *Goodbye Amigo Bill: Researching His Ghost Uncovered a Classified Grandpa*.

Bill works Tuesday–Saturday 12–6pm and Sunday 12–4pm (closed Mondays) and conducts research during slow periods at the store. His IT background informs a methodical, documentation-focused approach. All of Ivert's original medals, uniform, and memorabilia were lost when his widow Arbutus — during a period of cognitive decline — put everything at the curb for trash. Items in Bill's shadow box are reissued replacements. Bill's mother (Robbie Lou Shinske, b. July 14, 1948, turning 78 in July 2026) lives with Bill but is emotionally unable to discuss her father and is not a research resource.

**Critical research protocol (non-negotiable):** All findings must be explicitly labeled **CONFIRMED** (from documents), **REASONABLE INFERENCE** (logical conclusion from evidence), or **SPECULATION** (hypothesis without direct evidence). Bill enforces this strictly and corrects immediately when it drifts. Never let speculation drift into assumed fact.

---

**Subject profile: Ivert Francis Shinske**

- **Service numbers:** W-2107178 (WO), AF6761734 (enlisted), AF 44 005 446 (appeared on May 5, 1956 re-enlistment certificate — SPECULATION: possibly temporary administrative number for final re-enlistment processing or transcription error; primary numbers remain the first two)
- **Vital dates:** Born November 5, 1907, Rock Island, IL (1908 appears in some retirement docs — conflict unresolved; 1907 considered more authoritative from casualty report). Died February 13, 1971, US Naval Hospital Orlando (former Orlando AFB, transferred to Navy by 1971)
- **Cause of death CONFIRMED:** Bronchogenic carcinoma, metastatic to mediastinal lymph nodes and esophagus. Casualty assistance officer: G.M. Pitts, MSgt, USAF, McCoy AFB FL. Buried civilian cemetery Orlando. Flag presented February 17, 1971
- **Physical description CONFIRMED:** Approx. 6'0" (range 5'11"–6'1" across documents), blue eyes, brown hair, 162 lbs, Blood Type O. (1926 exam recorded grey eyes — likely a recording variation)
- **SSN:** 265-52-8360
- **Pre-military occupation:** Electrician
- **Education:** Ottawa High School, Ottawa, IL (not Rock Island). Post-graduate mathematics, Mt. Clemens
- **Family:**
  - Wife: Arbutus M. Shinske, married October 3, 1931, Mt. Clemens, Michigan. Dependency established September 28, 1950. Died 2007 at age 99
  - Daughter: Robbie Lou Shinske, born July 14, 1948 (Bill's mother)
  - Father: Frank A. Shinske, 190 Elm Ave, Elmhurst, IL (formerly Frank Apollo Shinske, b. 1882, LaSalle, IL)
  - Mother: Estella Pearl Shinske, 607 3rd Street, Savannah, IL
  - Pre-war home: Mt. Clemens, Michigan
  - Permanent family address: 928 W. Yale Ave, Orlando, FL
- **Ancestry:** Original surname likely Wyszynski. Line traces: Fabiano (b. 1750 Germany, wife Magdalena Siemierkowska) → Laurentius (b. 1775 Poland, m. Agnes Sobkowiak 1804, Kolo Wielkopolskie) → Valentine (b. 1814, m. Katherine Sophia Stanoch) → Frank (b. 1850 Posen Germany, m. Anna Rose Schmith) → Frank Apollo (b. 1882 LaSalle, IL) → Ivert. **Brick wall at Fabiano**
- **Personal interests:** Football, baseball, track, basketball, softball, bowling, wrestling, tennis, boxing. Hobbies: hunting and fishing. Licensed to drive auto, 6x6 truck, motorcycle (Florida license)
- **NSLI policy:** N-9750912, $9,000 by 1951
